Title: A Simple Ally as a Vampire Rule?

Messages.Author: jspektr
Messages.Body:
With all the hoopla over the allies going to torpor business, wouldn't
it just be FAR simpler to make a new ruling that doesn't produce this
situation?

The problem seems to be that "as a vampire" is unclear, because it
doesn't specify which ally traits are retained, and which ones are
lost. Apparently having life instead of blood, burning at zero life,
etc. are retained, but treating aggravated damage as normal is not.

Would it not be simpler to just say "can play cards a vampire of
capacity X with basic Y can play" instead of "as a vampire"?

Really, isn't that easier? It allows them to play any card a vampire
of the right capacity, with the right discipline could play, and
neatly sidesteps all concerns over the effects of the card. Nowhere
does it say they are treated as a vampire, it doesn't make them
suddenly vulnerable to things they were not vulnerable to before, and
doesn't result in weird situations like Allies in torpor.

I know similar ideas have been brought up, but I'm trying to proprose
something even simpler, that only takes a single line to explain.

JSpektr

Messages.Author: jspektr
Messages.Body:
LSJ <vte...@white-wolf.com> wrote in message news:<3CDA6BD9...@white-wolf.com>...

> jspektr wrote:
> > Would it not be simpler to just say "can play cards a vampire of
> > capacity X with basic Y can play" instead of "as a vampire"?
>
> See http://groups.google.com/groups?selm=3CD29FE7.42F322B1%40white-wolf.com
> for the counter-argument to this proposal.

Perhaps I was unclear, but that counter-argument does not apply here.

Give the ally the ability to play any card playable by a vampire that
has X discipline and Y capacity. This means they can play cards
refering specifically to vampires (I'm not sure what part of "playable
by a vampire" is not clear?).

I think you're trying to say that giving them the ability to play a
card playable by a vampire means that if the card gives a benefit to
"this vampire" then they would not get the benefit, because they are
not "this vampire." That seems like needlessly splitting hairs. If you
want to include "can play cards a vampire that has X discipline and Y
capacity can play, all effects of that card are applied to this ally"
then you could. That would overrule the "this vampire" text.

If you really want to cover all your bases, I guess it could be "can
play cards a vampire that has X discipline and Y capacity can play,
all references to the acting vampire are considered to refer to this
ally". That still seems awfully wordy, but far better (to me) than the
existing ruling, as it stays true to the original designer's intent,
keeps within the spirit of the game and the RPG, and requires less
explaining.

JSpektr

Messages.Author: Chris Berger
Messages.Body:
"jspektr" <jsp...@sprynet.com> wrote in message
news:196f2577.02050...@posting.google.com...

> With all the hoopla over the allies going to torpor business, wouldn't
> it just be FAR simpler to make a new ruling that doesn't produce this
> situation?
>

My preference has always been that when an ally plays discipline cards "as a
vampire", all instances of "this vampire" are considered to refer to "this
minion." Simple, easy, doesn't require any of the strangeness that's been
going on lately. Not that I'm gonna whine about it because, again, who cares?
Allies suck, and the ones that can play discipline cards are almost uniformly
overcosted.

Personally, I would extend the "this minion" effect even to permanent cards
that would go on the ally and always treat it as they would normally treat a
vampire who played them, but that's not really a necessary effect.

Well put, and more concise. LSJ has said this is under review, we can
all hope the result is something like this, clear, concise and simple.

That being said, we should try and break this suggestion now, so we
can find any flaws *before* official rulings are made.

JSpektr - has it been considered that maybe the rules team, with their
very deep knowledge of the rules, is perhaps too close to the trees to
see the forest? They don't seem to have anticipated the current
uproar, over either the changes to allies or to Roteschreck/interupt
effects. I don't mean to offend, but perhaps some perspective would go
a long way towards avoiding such problems in the future.
